'''Christopher Ian Byrnes''' (June 28, 1949 – February 7, 2010) was an American [[Mathematics|mathematician]] and [[Control theory|control theorist]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Christopher I. Byrnes [Obituaries] |journal=IEEE Control Systems Magazine |date=October 2010 |volume=30 |issue=5 |pages=84–87 |doi=10.1109/MCS.2010.937817 |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stamp/stamp.jsp?arnumber=5575556 |access-date=12 February 2026 |issn=1941-000X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was the Edward H. and Florence G. Skinner Professor Emeritus of Systems Science and Mathematics at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] and served as dean of the School of Engineering & Applied Science from 1991 to 2006.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lutz |first1=Diana |title=Chris Byrnes, former dean of engineering, dies at 60 |url=https://source.washu.edu/2010/02/chris-byrnes-former-dean-of-engineering-dies-at-60/ |access-date=12 February 2026 |work=The Source |publisher=Washington University in St. Louis |date=14 February 2010}}</ref>

Byrnes made foundational contributions to [[nonlinear control]], output regulation, [[distributed parameter system]]s, and geometric methods in control theory.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hu |first1=Xiaoming |last2=Jonsson |first2=Ulf |last3=Wahlberg |first3=Bo |last4=Ghosh |first4=Bijoy |title=Three Decades of Progress in Control Sciences: Dedicated to Chris Byrnes and Anders Lindquist |date=29 October 2010 |publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-642-11277-5 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Three_Decades_of_Progress_in_Control_Sci/tuSvDAEACAAJ?hl=en |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Together with [[Tryphon T. Georgiou]] and [[Anders Lindquist]], Byrnes was a founder of the so-called Byrnes–Georgiou–Lindquist school, which developed a new moment-based approach for the solution of control and estimation problems with complexity constraints.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Aulisa |first1=Eugenio |last2=Gilliam |first2=David |title=A Practical Guide to Geometric Regulation for Distributed Parameter Systems |date=18 June 2015 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=978-1-4822-4014-6 |edition=XIII |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/A_Practical_Guide_to_Geometric_Regulatio/spHYCQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&pg=PA263&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Byrnes was born in [[New York City]] in 1950 and raised in [[the Bronx]]. He earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in mathematics from [[Manhattan College]] in 1971. As a freshman, he encountered his first computer and briefly worked as an economic forecaster for the [[United Nations]], troubleshooting computer code. He declined a permanent position to continue his studies.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chris byrnes |url=https://www.math.ttu.edu/~gilliam/ttu/cib_mem_webpage/Chris_Byrnes_Workshop/Workshop.html |website=www.math.ttu.edu |publisher=Texas Tech University |access-date=12 February 2026}}</ref>

He attended the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst|University of Massachusetts, Amherst]], where he studied [[differential geometry]] under [[Marshall H. Stone]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Technical Abstract Bulletin |date=1971 |publisher=Defense Documentation Center. |page=129 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Technical_Abstract_Bulletin/-fgRAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&pg=PA129&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He earned a [[Master of Science]] degree in 1973 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate]] in mathematics in 1975 with a dissertation on the algebraic foundations of differential geometry.<ref>{{cite book |title=Algebraic Geometric Methods for the Stabilizability and Reliability of Multivariable and of Multimode Systems |date=1983 |pages=41; 89 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Algebraic_Geometric_Methods_for_the_Stab/QSNNAQAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=christopher+i.+byrnes&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Nichols |first1=N. K. |last2=Owens |first2=David H. |title=The Mathematics of Control Theory: Based on the Proceedings of a Conference on Control Theory, Organized by the Institute of Mathematics and Its Applications, and Held at the University of Strathclyde in September 1988 |date=1992 |publisher=Clarendon Press |isbn=978-0-19-853640-6 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Mathematics_of_Control_Theory/9vpQAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=christopher+i.+byrnes&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Byrnes began his academic career as an instructor of mathematics at the [[University of Utah]] in 1975. He joined [[Harvard University]] in 1978 as an assistant professor and attained tenure as an associate professor in 1983. He later taught at [[Arizona State University]], where he founded the Center for Systems Engineering Research. In 1989, he joined [[Washington University in St. Louis]] as professor of systems and control, and later served as chair of the Department of Systems Science and Control.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lutz |first1=Diana |title=Chris Byrnes, former dean of engineering, dies at 60 |url=https://source.washu.edu/2010/02/chris-byrnes-former-dean-of-engineering-dies-at-60/ |website=The Source |access-date=12 February 2026 |date=14 February 2010}}</ref>

On July 15, 1991, Byrnes became the eighth dean of the School of Engineering & Applied Science at Washington University. During his tenure, the school's endowment grew from $54 million to $185 million, and endowed professorships increased from nine to 37. He oversaw the founding of the Department of Biomedical Engineering, the Institute of Biological and Medical Engineering, and the implementation of Project 21, a strategic planning initiative at the university.

His research spanned [[systems science]], control theory, and [[applied mathematics]], with major contributions in [[nonlinear control]], output regulation, [[distributed parameter system]]s, and the geometric and algebraic foundations of control.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Desch |first1=Wolfgang |last2=Kappel |first2=Franz |last3=Kunisch |first3=Karl |title=Control and Estimation of Distributed Parameter Systems: Nonlinear Phenomena: International Conference in Vorau (Austria), July 18–24, 1993 |date=6 December 2012 |publisher=Birkhäuser |isbn=978-3-0348-8530-0 |pages=62–77 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Control_and_Estimation_of_Distributed_Pa/yIb1BwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&pg=PA77&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> In the late 1970s and 1980s, he developed the nonlinear regulator equations and extended output regulation theory to nonlinear and distributed systems, including boundary control and [[partial differential equation]]s.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bowers |first1=Kenneth L. |last2=Lund |first2=John |title=Computation and Control II: Proceedings of the Second Bozeman Conference, Bozeman, Montana, August 1–7, 1990 |date=27 November 2013 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4612-0427-5 |pages=45–61 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Computation_and_Control_II/ikoOBwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&pg=PA61&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He contributed to the generalized [[servomechanism]] problem, [[zero dynamics]], and [[Root locus analysis|root locus]] methods for infinite-dimensional systems.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hilton |first1=P. J. |author-link=Peter Hilton |last2=Young |first2=G. S. |title=New Directions in Applied Mathematics: Papers Presented April 25/26, 1980, on the Occasion of the Case Centennial Celebration |date=6 December 2012 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4612-5651-9 |pages=60–64; 70 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/New_Directions_in_Applied_Mathematics/nojuBwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&pg=PA70&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

He collaborated extensively with researchers including [[Alberto Isidori]], Anders Lindquist, and Tryphon T. Georgiou, with whom he established the so-called Byrnes–Georgiou–Lindquist school. Their research developed moment-based methods for control and estimation under complexity constraints used widely in the field.<ref>{{cite book |title=Applied Mechanics Reviews |date=1987 |publisher=American Society of Mechanical Engineers |page=597 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Applied_Mechanics_Reviews/AOctLz5ZY7AC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=christopher+i.+byrnes&pg=PA597&printsec=frontcover |access-date=12 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> His work also impacted [[Kalman filter]]ing, [[robust control]], pole placement, multivariable [[Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem]], and generalized moment problems. Applications include [[signal processing]], [[electric power system]]s, and [[speech synthesis]].

At the time of his death in 2010, Byrnes was a distinguished visiting professor in optimization and systems theory at the [[Royal Institute of Technology]] in [[Stockholm]], Sweden. He had previously held visiting and adjunct appointments at the institute from 1985 to 1991 and 2001.<ref>{{cite web |title=Christopher I. Byrnes |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010ICSys..30e..84./abstract |website=IEEE Control Systems |publisher=Harvard Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory |access-date=12 February 2026 |pages=84–87 |language=en |doi=10.1109/MCS.2010.937817 |date=2010}}</ref>

==Awards==
* Honorary Doctor of Technology, [[Royal Institute of Technology]], 1998
* Foreign Member, [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]], 2001
* Fellow, [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE)
* IEEE George Axelby Prize (twice)
* [[W. T. and Idalia Reid Prize]], 2005
* IEEE [[Hendrik W. Bode Lecture Prize]], 2008<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.ttu.edu/~gilliam/ttu/cib_mem_webpage/Chris_Byrnes_Workshop/Workshop.html|title=Workshop in Celebration of the Life, Mathematics and Memories of Christopher I. Byrnes|website=ttu.edu|access-date=19 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://source.wustl.edu/2010/02/chris-byrnes-former-dean-of-engineering-dies-at-60/|title=Chris Byrnes, former dean of engineering, dies at 60|website=wustl.edu|date=14 February 2010}}</ref>
